science.title: Radiation pulse in an optically thin 2D medium — free-streaming M1 transport
science.mechanism: A Gaussian radiation-temperature pulse released in a nearly transparent medium (scattering 1e-6, no absorption) on a 200x200 Cartesian grid: the radiation must stream freely at the speed of light and its peak must decay as 1/r. The gas is essentially passive; the row exercises the hyperbolic radiation subsystem (Src/Radiation/rad_flux.c, rad_hllc.c) with a three-equation implicit system.
science.distinct_from_other_rows: Only row in the optically thin limit where the radiation transport, not the gas–radiation coupling, is the whole test; radiation solver HLLC with gas TVDLF.
science.failure_modes_exposed: A wrong free-streaming eigenvalue (|F|/E -> 1 limit of the M1 closure) or a wrong radiation HLLC gives a pulse that propagates at the wrong speed or with the wrong 1/r decay.
references: Melon Fuksman, J. D. & Mignone, A. 2019, ApJS 242, 20 (radiative transfer module for relativistic MHD in PLUTO)
Sadowski, A., Narayan, R., Tchekhovskoy, A. & Zhu, Y. 2013, MNRAS 429, 3533 (M1 closure semi-implicit scheme)

policy.active_rule: abs(candidate - reference) <= 1e-12 + 1e-8 * abs(reference) for every finite value of every declared raw binary64 DBL payload and frame; byte-identical payloads take a fast path; shape/frame/artifact/finite gates are hard gates.
policy.active_rule_status: owner-approved provisional combined tolerance shared by every row of this suite (same rule as the merged pluto-mhd-les suite); not a row-calibrated scientific error bar.
policy.case_specific_policy_shape: Pulse front radius versus time (should be c*t); peak E_r decay law; isotropy; radiation energy conservation as a secondary gate.
policy.evidence_required_before_numeric_bound: Two reproducible incumbent runs; genuinely different correct binaries (compiler/ISA/FMA); a resolution or replication study of the named observables; at least one plausible porting defect that the policy rejects; and a recorded owner decision.
policy.determinism_note: One-rank incumbent reruns are expected to be byte-identical. The radiation implicit step (Src/Radiation/rad_step.c, newtonsolve.c) iterates to RADIATION_ERROR=1e-7 with RADIATION_MAXITER=200, so the number of operations depends on floating-point convergence tests: a correct port with different rounding can legitimately take a different iteration count. Together with the RHD primitive-recovery Newton loop this is a DEFER/MEASURED-class hazard under references/determinism-triage.md; the provisional elementwise rule is therefore provisional, and calibration must measure the correct-build band before any bound is called scientific.

output_contract.format_family: PLUTO 'dbl' static-grid output convention (this row's shipped deck's [Static Grid Output] stanza selects dbl in single_file mode).
expected_markers: data.<NNNN>.dbl (per-dump snapshot; NNNN zero-padded frame index)
output_contract.frames: initial dump data.0000.dbl at t=0 plus 1 dump(s) every 35.0 time units ending at tstop=35.0 (final dump coincides with the last interval)
output_contract.byte_layout: grid.out (Src/set_grid.c) is ASCII: header comment lines, then 3 per-axis blocks each '<N>' followed by N lines '<i> <xl> <xr>' (interior points, ghosts excluded). dbl.out (Src/write_data.c) is ASCII, one line per dump: '<nfile> <time> <dt> <step> <single_file|multiple_files> <little|big> <name1> <name2> ...'. data.<NNNN>.dbl (Src/bin_io.c FileWriteData) is raw float64 with no header, native byte order, variable-major, x-fastest within each variable block, interior zones only. Variable names come from Src/var_names.c; radiation rows append enr, fr1, fr2, fr3 after the fluid block (Src/RHD/mod_defs.h, Src/HD/mod_defs.h, Src/MHD/mod_defs.h, Src/RMHD/mod_defs.h index macros). tests/checks/*/validate.py implements exactly this layout and compares every retained finite value.

criteria.name: dbl_payload_equivalence
criteria.note: Applied to every finite raw binary64 value of every declared frame; the first violation fails the row with frame/index/variable diagnostics.
